messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated KV cache eviction + continuous-batching growth detected on longrope-ntk pool (region: us-west-2). 90th p90 latency for text-gen is up ~3x, error rate rising. Pager sent to #incidents.
eli: seeing it on dashboards too — prefetch miss rate spiked, rope KV size jumped ~6x in last 10m.
maya: omg customers on Dedicated are reporting timeouts. any initial blast radius?
tony_sre: I'm oncall — taking. tagging @grace_prod for Dedicated/Customer context. can you dump recent deploys?
grace_prod: no prod deploys in last 30m from our side. we did flip a config in ntk-worker earlier today (sliding-window enable).
eli: that matches. sliding-window + longer prefetched contexts increased KV cardinality. continuous batching kept holding onto larger KV prefixes -> memory + eviction storms.
opsbot: command run: `redwood infra metrics query --range 15m --query "kv.evictions{pool:longrope-ntk}"` -> evictions: 112k, prev 2k.
tony_sre: OK first actions: 1) disable sliding-window on longrope-ntk (hot config rollback), 2) reduce batch.max_tokens from 2048 -> 768 to reduce KV retention, 3) enable backpressure throttle on prefetcher to shed new longctx requests. doing step 1 now.
eli: rolling rollback group to ntk pool (annotating canary nodes). patch: `reconfig longrope-ntk --set sliding_window=false --reason "eviction storm mitigation"`
maya: ETA on that? some customers seeing 502s.
tony_sre: rollback started at 1729123502. applying to 25% nodes first. watch logs.
(1 minute later)
eli: notices: eviction rate dropped 20% after first 25% rolled back. good signal.
cs-alyssa: letting affected customers know — seeing errors from 3 enterprise tenants, primarily embedded chat endpoints. Tiers: Dedicated + Reserved.
opsbot: command run: `redwood infra config get longrope-ntk` -> sliding_window: false (partial), batch.max_tokens: 2048 (still).
tony_sre: lowering batch sizes now across canary: `for node in canary; do set batch.max_tokens=768; done` -- kicking.
grace_prod: also enable temporary KV eviction buffer policy to prefer small prefixes: `kv.policy = prefer_small_prefixes` (hot).
eli: adding backpressure rule: new requests with expected KV > 1MB will get 429 until stabilizes. applying via routing policy.
maya: metrics: p90 latency trending down from 3x to 1.6x after both patches. error rate still above baseline (~1.8% now vs baseline 0.2%).
ton y_sre: typo in handle — re-post: tony_sre: error rate now 1.8% — still elevated. working on traffic shaping to reduce tail.
(10 minutes later)
eli: after forcing prefetch throttle we see cache growth flattening. KV size peaked ~18GB per node, now decaying. continuous-batch queue depth reduced.
opsbot: recent logs (excerpt): ```[2024-05-19T14:12:32Z] worker=ntk-22 WARN kv_cache_evicted=4098 keys=22456 prefetched_ctx=12MB```
maya: customer impact note: three Dedicated tenants saw 5-15 minute elevated latencies/timeouts during peak. Hosted route customers saw degraded p95 but automatic fallbacks triggered for some routes so degraded gracefully.
ton y_sre: (again fixing keyboard) tony_sre: I'm going to promote these fixes cluster-wide once we hit 30m steady decline. notifying infra-runbook owners.
cs-alyssa: sending proactive status emails to affected accounts, include mitigation steps and ETA for postmortem.
eli: small hotfix commit with changelog: "ntk: disable sliding-window by default for longrope pools; add prefetch size guard; lower default batch.max_tokens for longctx-prone models". prepping canary deploy.
grace_prod: also opened gate on long context feature flags; will require explicit opt-in per tenant for >8k tokens until followup.
opsbot: deploy started at 1729123690 -> canary nodes updated.
(20 minutes later)
eli: metrics stable for 12m; evictions back near baseline. KV memory trending down to normal. latency p95 dropped to ~1.05x baseline.
ton y_sre: promoting to 100% now. executing global config change across ntk pools. note: this will be reversible.
maya: monitoring customer queues; CS has templates ready for outreach.
(after completion)
opsbot: global config change completed at 1729123875.
eli: final customer impact summary for now: - Window: 14:10—14:25 UTC (~15 min peak) - Impacted: 3 Dedicated tenants reported timeouts; ~0.6% of total hosted requests saw p95 > 500ms; error spike to 1.8% at peak - Root cause: sliding-window + long-prefetch combos caused KV cardinality explosion + continuous batching retention -> eviction storms and latency cliff - Mitigation: disabled sliding-window for longrope-ntk, lowered batch.max_tokens, enabled prefetch backpressure, set temporary KV eviction bias - Current status: stable, monitoring 1h for regressions.
grace_prod: raising follow-up action items: 1) design longctx admission control (limit prefetch size per request), 2) model/route tagging to opt-in sliding-window, 3) improve chaos tests to simulate continuous-batch + longctx, 4) add metric alerts for kv.cardinality growth.
ton y_sre: will open incident ticket and assign owners; I'll draft immediate postmortem outline.
cs-alyssa: have comms draft ready; will coordinate with legal for any contract impact notes.
eli: thanks team. assigning post-incident review: owners: tony_sre (ops lead), eli (runtime), grace_prod (product gating), maya (monitoring). Please add timeline and play-by-play to the doc.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Handoff complete. Please update #postmortems with the incident ID: INC-20240519-0847 and link to the runbook notes.
